title: What does CheckCash do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of CheckCash and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, CheckCash lets the named destination redeem an XRPL Check, subject to the sender's available funds and payment liquidity. [1]

The receiver specifies either a requested Amount or a minimum acceptable DeliverMin according to the transaction rules. A Check is not a guarantee that funds were reserved. Failed cashing can leave it available for another attempt; inspect the validated outcome before crediting the customer or assuming it disappeared. [1]

The CheckCash reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using CheckCash, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
